questions.text: A company ships €4m of goods on 30 December; the customer obtains control that day and pays on 15 January. Assuming the other IFRS 15 criteria are met, the December accounts should show:

options.a: €4m revenue and a corresponding receivable.
options.b: Recognize €4m as other comprehensive income rather than revenue because the receivable has not yet been collected.
options.c: No revenue until the January cash settlement.
options.d: Recognize a €4m contract asset and no revenue until the last collection date, independent of transfer.
options.e: €4m cash and a corresponding contract liability.
options.f: €4m revenue and immediate financing cash flow.

questions.text: A seller receives cash in advance for a service that will be provided evenly over six months. Which revenue-recognition approach is most consistent with IFRS 15?

options.a: Recognize one-sixth of the revenue immediately upon signing and the remainder when the last payment arrives, regardless of service delivery.
options.b: Defer recognizing any liability until the firm incurs its first operating expense.
options.c: Recognize revenue entirely when the customer transfers advance cash.
options.d: Recognize revenue when the service provider pays its own employees.
options.e: Recognize revenue only once all six monthly services are completed.
options.f: Recognize revenue over the service period as the obligation is satisfied.

questions.text:
Consider the statements.
I. A contract price may need allocation across multiple promises.
II. Cash collection is necessary before any revenue can be recognized.
III. IFRS 15 requires identifying distinct performance obligations.
Which set is correct?

options.a: None of I, II or III
options.b: I and II only
options.c: I and III only
options.d: II and III only

questions.text: A firm sells equipment with a standalone price of €90,000 and a two-year support package with a standalone price of €10,000 for a total bundle price of €80,000. What amount is initially allocated to the equipment?

options.a: €80,000, because the total transaction price is attributed entirely to the equipment.
options.b: €64,000, because the allocation is based on an assumed 80% performance-completion rate.

questions.text: A contract contains three promises, but only one has been satisfied by year-end. What determines revenue recognized so far?

options.a: The full amount of cash expected over the contract's duration.
options.b: The entire contract value once the contract becomes enforceable.
options.c: The transaction-price allocation to the promise already satisfied.
options.d: The supplier's total production cost for the three promises.

questions.text: A producer's reported revenue rises by 12%, yet its main geographic segment contracts. Which disclosure most directly helps reconcile this observation?

options.a: Aggregate sales figures for the group, without any separate discussion of geographic segment performance.
options.b: The maturity schedule of bonds, irrespective of changes in business operations.
options.c: Segment reporting by geography or product, including contributions from other segments.
options.d: Aggregate depreciation alone, irrespective of the firm's product categories.
options.e: Nominal common-share par value, irrespective of where the company operates.

questions.text:
Consider the statements.
I. Segment reporting can distinguish revenue streams across business units.
II. Common-size income statements express items relative to sales.
III. A trend analysis compares only competitors within a single financial year.
Which set is correct?

options.a: I, II and III
options.b: III only
options.c: I and II only
options.d: II only

questions.text: A firm reports sales of €1,200m, COGS €690m and SG&A €270m. Which pair is correct?

options.a: Gross margin 42.5%; SG&A-to-sales 30.0%
options.b: Gross margin 42.5%; SG&A-to-sales 22.5%
options.c: Gross margin 42.5%; SG&A-to-sales 18.5%
options.d: Gross margin 57.5%; SG&A-to-sales 30.0%

questions.text: A company reports a year-on-year improvement in net profit margin entirely because it sold a subsidiary at a large gain. How should an analyst treat this when forecasting future operations?

options.a: Assume the entire margin improvement will recur every period indefinitely.
options.b: Separate the gain and examine recurring profitability from continuing activities.
options.c: Treat the disposal gain as additional sales in each future forecast year.
options.d: Exclude the firm's continuing operations because they are temporary.

questions.text:
Consider the statements.
I. Discontinued operations can include a disposed unit's profit before sale.
II. They can also include the gain or loss realized on disposing of that unit.
III. Any ordinary small asset disposal is automatically a discontinued operation.
Which set is correct?

options.a: I and II only
options.b: I and III only
options.c: I only
options.d: I, II and III

questions.text: A company disposes of an entire business line that represented one-third of revenue. Which feature most supports discontinued-operation presentation?

options.a: Cash proceeds from the disposal exceed the original purchase price.
options.b: The sold assets had been depreciated in earlier financial statements.
options.c: The disposal represents a strategic shift with a major effect on the company.
options.d: The sold assets are non-current and therefore incapable of recurring revenue.

questions.text: A firm cuts R&D expenses aggressively just before year-end. This boosts current earnings, but no pipeline projects have been completed. What is the key concern?

options.a: R&D cuts necessarily increase reported capitalized development assets.
options.b: Current income may improve at the expense of future competitive capacity.
options.c: Future revenue is guaranteed because development spending has fallen.
options.d: Current earnings must decrease because research is always a cash asset.

questions.text: Under IAS 38, a company conducts fundamental research and later achieves a development phase meeting all capitalization criteria. Which general treatment is appropriate?

options.a: Expense research; capitalize qualifying development expenditure prospectively.
options.b: Expense all research and development irrespective of feasibility evidence.
options.c: Any project intended to create intellectual property must be capitalized from the moment researchers are hired.
options.d: Capitalize all prior research retroactively once development becomes feasible.
options.e: Capitalize all research; expense qualifying development expenditure.
options.f: Under IFRS, research spending is capitalized once management expects success, while all development spending is expensed.

questions.text:
Consider the statements.
I. A reduction in R&D intensity always proves product-development efficiency.
II. SG&A may include salaries, marketing and administrative overheads.
III. Reducing SG&A can raise profits even without higher sales.
Which set is correct?

options.a: I and III only
options.b: I only
options.c: II and III only
options.d: None of I, II or III

questions.text: An analyst compares two pharmaceutical companies' reported R&D expenses. One capitalizes a larger proportion of qualifying development spending. What additional disclosure would best improve comparability?

options.a: Gross selling prices alone, because development policy cannot affect reported income.
options.b: Development costs capitalized, amortization charged and new projects in the pipeline.
options.c: Common-share par value alone, because capitalization is equivalent to an equity issue.
options.d: Customer receivables alone, because capitalization changes only cash collection periods.

questions.text: A company has net income attributable to ordinary shareholders of €90m and a weighted-average 30m basic shares. Basic EPS equals:
A firm reports basic EPS of €4.00 and diluted EPS of €3.70. Which explanation is most consistent with this difference?

options.a: Potential conversion of outstanding instruments would increase the earnings claim per share denominator.
options.b: The firm repurchased all outstanding shares before the fiscal year began.
options.c: An increase in per-share dividends directly causes the weighted-average share count to fall.
options.d: Other comprehensive income was reclassified automatically into ordinary revenue.

questions.text:
Consider the statements.
I. Convertible debt may affect diluted EPS.
II. Diluted EPS must exceed basic EPS whenever options are outstanding.
III. Employee share options may create dilution.
Which set is correct?

options.a: III only
options.b: I and III only
options.c: I and II only
options.d: II and III only

questions.text: Employees exercise options at €18 when the company's shares trade at €46. For each exercised option, the lecture's measure of value transferred to the option holder is:
Which distinction best describes basic EPS versus diluted EPS?

options.a: Basic EPS includes all potential shares; diluted EPS counts only issued common shares.
options.b: Basic EPS uses end-of-year shares rather than weighted-average shares; diluted EPS uses cash proceeds from stock options as earnings.
options.c: Basic EPS uses beginning shares; diluted EPS uses the highest daily market share price.
options.d: Basic EPS uses existing weighted-average common shares; diluted EPS considers relevant potential shares.
options.e: Basic EPS includes OCI; diluted EPS is determined solely by cash from operations.
options.f: Basic EPS uses all potentially dilutive shares immediately, while diluted EPS excludes convertible shares until actual conversion.

questions.text: A parent reports net income €100m and OCI loss €35m. Distributions to shareholders are €15m. What is total comprehensive income?

Consider the statements.
I. OCI always equals cash generated by financing activities.
II. Foreign currency translation adjustments can affect OCI.
III. Certain hedging gains or losses can affect OCI.
Which set is correct?

options.a: I and III only
options.b: I, II and III
options.c: I and II only
options.d: II and III only

questions.text: A firm's foreign subsidiary has increased euro-denominated net asset value solely because of exchange-rate movements. Under the lecture's discussion, the associated unrealized translation adjustment is commonly reported:

options.a: as a cash receipt from customers in operations.
options.b: in OCI, rather than as ordinary net income.
options.c: as a reduction in the debt principal outstanding.
options.d: as an increase in net payout to shareholders.

questions.text: A company recognizes a net gain on a qualifying cash-flow hedge in OCI. Which statement is most accurate?

options.a: An OCI gain must increase reported net income immediately because comprehensive income and net income are identical.
options.b: The gain must be reported as a new cash inflow from issuing ordinary shares.
options.c: Comprehensive income can change although the gain does not enter net income immediately.
options.d: The gain cannot affect equity until the derivative contract is sold for cash.
options.e: Net income and comprehensive income must both rise by exactly the gain immediately.

questions.text: The income statement of a manufacturer shows sales of €2,400m and operating expenses of €2,160m. An analyst wants to compare its cost structure with a peer with €600m sales. Which transformation is appropriate?

options.a: Divide the income statement by share capital to remove differences in company size.
options.b: Divide each operating expense by the peer's total liabilities instead of revenue.
options.c: Express each operating expense as a percentage of the firm's own revenue.
options.d: Compare expense amounts in euros without correcting for the difference in scale.

questions.text: Revenue rises by 8%, while gross profit rises by only 2%. Which conclusion can be drawn without further information?

options.a: The gross profit margin has increased relative to the previous year.
options.b: Operating cash flow has increased by exactly the same amount as revenue.
options.c: The gross profit margin has decreased relative to the previous year.
options.d: The gross profit margin is unchanged because a rise in both revenue and gross profit always cancels out.
options.e: The company has necessarily increased its basic earnings per share.
options.f: The company’s gross margin rises by six percentage points, because its gross profit has increased.

questions.text: A company records a one-off restructuring charge of €90m and later reverses an excessive provision. Which analyst concern is closest to the lecture's earnings-quality discussion?

options.a: Reversing a provision necessarily produces an equal cash receipt from customers.
options.b: Restructuring provisions are always classified as equity and excluded from profit.
options.c: Any restructuring charge guarantees permanent future cost reductions of the same amount.
options.d: A large current charge may depress today's earnings and inflate subsequent reported growth.

questions.text:
Consider the statements.
I. Research expenditures generally lower current accounting profit when incurred.
II. Qualifying development expenditures may be capitalized and later amortized.
III. A high reported R&D expense necessarily means zero innovation output.
Which set is correct?

options.a: I and III only
options.b: II only
options.c: I and II only
options.d: II and III only

questions.text: A firm reports current net income €175m and comprehensive income €120m. Which inference follows directly?

options.a: Other comprehensive income is +€55m.
options.b: Cash used in investing activities is €55m.
options.c: Other comprehensive income is −€55m.
options.d: Dividends to common shareholders are €55m.

questions.text: A firm recognizes substantial revenue in December while receivables age rapidly and CFO falls. Which follow-up is most important for assessing earnings quality?

options.a: Whether net income can be reclassified in full as OCI without further review.
options.b: Whether contractual obligations were fulfilled and collection assumptions remain credible.
options.c: Whether all sales were made to customers within the same geographic region.
options.d: Whether it can issue new shares to replace every unpaid customer invoice.

questions.text: A company sells a material business unit at a gain and reports both continuing and discontinued results. Which figure is generally more informative about next year's recurring operating performance?

options.a: Profit from continuing operations after separating transient disposal effects.
options.b: Gross cash received from the sale regardless of the remaining operations.
options.c: Consolidated profit including the gain, assumed to repeat at the same level.
options.d: Total share capital, because disposal gains never enter the income statement.

questions.text:
Consider the statements.
I. The accruals concept permits revenue without simultaneous cash collection.
II. Expense recognition need not coincide with cash disbursement.
III. Accrual accounting eliminates all room for management estimation.
Which set is correct?

options.a: II and III only
options.b: I and II only
options.c: I, II and III
options.d: I and III only

questions.text: A firm has €36m net income to common shareholders and 12m weighted-average shares. Later, warrants with exercise prices below market are exercised. Which issue matters for reported diluted EPS?

options.a: The additional shares automatically remove the need to calculate diluted EPS.
options.b: The warrants make gross profit the required numerator for basic and diluted EPS.
options.c: The warrants increase reported net income by the full stock market value on exercise.
options.d: The additional shares reduce the earnings attributable per common share, other factors held equal.

questions.text: Two otherwise identical firms perform equal research work, but one records some spending as capitalizable development after meeting the specified criteria. What is the near-term difference?

options.a: The capitalizing firm automatically has greater operating cash flow from the same payments.
options.b: The capitalizing firm may show higher current earnings and a larger asset balance.
options.c: The capitalizing firm must show lower current earnings and a smaller asset balance.
options.d: Both firms must show identical earnings because research is always fully capitalized.

questions.text:
Consider the statements.
I. Control transfer is a key element of revenue recognition under IFRS 15.
II. Revenue must always be paid before it can appear in the income statement.
III. Receiving cash in advance always satisfies every future performance obligation.
Which set is correct?

options.a: I and II only
options.b: III only
options.c: I only
options.d: II and III only

questions.text:
Consider the statements.
I. Dilutive securities may affect diluted EPS.
II. Other comprehensive income may change total equity without entering net income.
III. A change in product mix can change gross margin.
Which set is correct?

options.a: II and III only
options.b: I and III only
options.c: I only
options.d: I and II only
